placeName.zh-CN: 阿根廷内乌肯省圣马丁德洛斯安第斯（San Martín de los Andes）
placeName.en: San Martín de los Andes, Neuquén, Argentina

details.direction: San Martín de los Andes (RCM4) → Patagonian trails → San Martín de los Andes. The organiser has not published a point-by-point order for 2027.
details.distanceMethod: The official Spanish 100 Millas page and its English translation both give 160.3 km. No point table is published, so there is no cumulative-distance series to compare with.
details.elevationMethod: The official Spanish 100 Millas page and its English translation both give 9,221 m. The official 2026 100Mi Participant Guide gives the same 9,221 m and states an approximate maximum altitude of 1,959 m, while the official 2026 altitude profile labels Cumbre CE Colorado at 1,765 m and Cumbre Quechuquina at 1,650 m; those are different labels and are not merged. The 100 Millas page warns that the 2027 course is based on 2026 and may change, so all 2026 profile and guide values are a baseline, not a 2027 guarantee. The profile prints no cumulative descent; a D− of about 9,310 m can only be derived arithmetically from 9,221 + (740 − 651) and is not presented as an official figure.
details.attribution: Patagonia Run. The absence of geometry is the organiser's policy, not a failed collection: the official 2026 technical briefing states “No hay tracks GPS oficiales… No se comparten tracks del circuito”, the 2026 100Mi guide repeats that tracks are not shared, and the 2027 race pages publish no GPX. Private, military, institutional and community land is authorised only on race day, which the organiser gives as the reason for withholding tracks. This site therefore shows no track and does not reconstruct one. The 2026 100Mi guide's 20-row PAS/PAEX table and eight intermediate cut-offs are presented as a 2026 baseline only, because the 2027 page says the circuit is based on 2026 and may change.
